summary.headline: KEI Industries Q1 FY27 net sales rose 23% to INR3,185 crore and operating margin reached 12.43%, with EBITDA up 39.5%.
summary.overview: Net sales grew 23% YoY to INR3,185 crore, while domestic wire and cable sales rose 29% to INR2,784 crore. Operating (EBITDA) margin expanded to 13.04% from 11.49%, and PAT rose 40% to INR274 crore, helped by product mix (EHV, retail/dealer channel) and operating leverage. Exports fell to INR341 crore from INR375 crore because Middle East orders were not executed and US custom duty issues persisted. Management reiterated a 20%+ growth target, though it declined to raise guidance above that, and said the Sanand plant is ramping up slowly.

segments.name: Domestic wire and cable
segments.commentary: Sales INR2,784 crore, up 29% YoY. Retail/dealer channel share rose to 59% from about 51%; 2,128 active dealers as of 30 June.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Sales INR341 crore vs INR375 crore last year, hit by unexecuted Middle East orders and US customs duty issues. Management expects exports to recover for full year.

segments.name: Extra high-voltage (EHV) cable
segments.commentary: Sales INR186 crore, up 47% YoY. Management cites EHV operating margin of about 15%, vs about 10.5% for institutional LV/MV power cable, 11% retail and above 11% export.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Sales INR43 crore vs INR61 crore last year; PHV EPC execution sales INR18 crore. Management says EPC is no longer a large share, supporting gross margin.

guidance_outlook: Management targets value growth of 20%+ CAGR; in Q&A it said full-year growth would be around 24-25%, and the CMD said FY27 revenue growth would exceed 25%.
Operating margin guided at 11-12% for coming year after crossing the earlier 11% hurdle; management says quarterly fluctuation of 0.25-0.5% is normal.

Sanand revenue expected at INR1,500-2,000 crore in FY27 (CMD corrected a media figure of about INR3,000 crore); long-run Sanand capacity about INR6,000 crore, rising to about INR7,000 crore within 2 years after balancing equipment.
Export share target of 17-18% of revenue for FY27 (FY26 about 16%); management expects exports to grow about 50% in the remaining nine months.
Capex of INR600-700 crore per year for the next 3-4 years; new INR700 crore Salarpur (Bhiwadi) plant for LV/MV cable to be built over about 2 years. Sanand balance of about INR300 crore in FY27.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex payment INR191 crore, of which Sanand INR180 crore; cumulative Sanand spend INR1,722 crore against a INR2,000 crore project cost, with the balance to be spent over about the next 6 months.
Capacity utilisation in Q1: cable 72%, house wire 61%, stainless steel wire 91%, communication cable 45%. Sanand Phase 1 at about 50% utilisation as of the call.
Sanand EHV line (152-metre tower) to be commissioned by March 2027; INR1,300 crore of Sanand capacity is for EHV cable, and EHV is expected to contribute about 9-10% of added capacity revenue.
Salarpur (Bhiwadi) plant of about INR700 crore announced for LV/MV power cable; management said greenfield projects take about 2 years to build plus about 1 year to ramp.
Management expects Sanand to run at 70-75% utilisation next year; the INR100-200 crore balancing equipment will add INR1,000+ crore turnover.
demand_pricing: Order book INR4,292 crore: domestic cable INR2,400 crore, export INR822 crore, EHV INR793 crore, EPC INR271 crore.
Price pass-through is formula-based on copper content, not a fixed percentage; management confirmed cost inflation has been passed on.
Management attributes margin gains to product mix, export margin orders, retail mix and lower fixed cost as a share of sales, not to market share gains.
Management cited strong demand from data centres, power T&D, renewables, EV, railways, urban infrastructure, housing and thermal power construction.
Inventory build reflects Sanand ramp-up and about INR60-100 crore of finished goods reversed under Ind AS because export goods had not yet reached customers at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex grow slowly and what drove the sharp wire and cable margin rise from 12.4% to 13.6% quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said fixed costs did not rise with incremental sales, and product mix and export margin orders helped. He said the company has crossed its earlier sub-11% operating margin hurdle and expects 11-12% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing market share given industry volume growth near 33-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied losing share, citing strong demand and capacity constraints. It reiterated a 20%+ CAGR target and said it is not chasing 35-40% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sanand revenue guidance for FY27 and the capacity potential?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said FY27 Sanand revenue of INR1,500-2,000 crore, correcting a media figure of about INR3,000 crore. Management said the long-run potential is INR6,000 crore, rising to about INR7,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 20%+ guidance not raised given industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited capital allocation discipline, the need to fund capex for future capacity, and working capital limits. It said actual growth could exceed guidance but it would not give higher numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports fall and can they grow about 50% over the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said Middle East shipments were blocked and US orders stalled; shipments have resumed at high freight cost. He expects exports to grow to meet the 17-18% share target.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the house wire breakup dropped and what is the outlook for retail share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give product-wise sales because competitors use the data. It said retail is favoured for lower working capital needs, and the mix may shift with export orders.

risks_watch: Sanand ramp-up pace: Phase 1 at about 50% utilisation; management expects 70-75% utilisation next year and FY27 Sanand revenue of INR1,500-2,000 crore, with manpower and machine stabilisation cited as constraints.

Export recovery: Q1 exports fell to INR341 crore; full-year 17-18% export share needs about 50% growth over the remaining nine months, with Middle East shipments resuming at high freight cost and US duty issues unresolved.

Margin sustainability: management guides 11-12% operating margin, says quarterly swings of 0.25-0.5% are normal, and attributes gains to mix (EHV, retail), export margin orders and fixed-cost leverage.

Growth gap versus industry: management guides 20%+ CAGR and FY27 revenue growth above 25%, while the analyst cited industry volume and value growth of roughly 33-35%; management declined to raise guidance.

Capex and working capital: INR600-700 crore annual capex for 3-4 years plus the new INR700 crore Salarpur plant; inventory build and about INR60-100 crore of export finished goods reversed under Ind AS.
Other income falls YoY (interest income INR14.59 crore vs INR28.77 crore) as QIP cash is deployed; management did not give a product-wise house wire split.

We will be growing more than what we are guiding and we will be to the level of industry standard, but we don't want to give very high numbers. That is not our policy.

summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and margins, but deliberately conservative on guidance: management repeatedly declined to raise the 20%+ growth target despite analyst pressure, citing capital allocation discipline and capacity ramp-up. Evasive on product-wise sales breakdown and on the cause of the media-quoted Sanand figure, which it corrected to INR1,500-2,000 crore.
